head: 0e4fed526e8d7ec6e145d86446c8e9671a8bebdb
classification_reasons: Spec is tight: Flagged concerns is 'none', the single open question carried from intent.md (pre-check vs catch-and-reraise) is answered in spec.md's 'Open questions from intent' with a stated rationale (coding-standards rule 2), and Acceptance gives exact, checkable targets (the literal string 'whole must not be zero', the two named pre-existing tests still passing, pytest count 10, compileall and ruff healthy output).

Blast radius is small and below every routine threshold: plan.md's 'Files that change' lists exactly two files (tests/test_calc.py, sample_pkg/calc.py); no .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml touched; no sdlc.yaml risk_list item (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) applies to a pure in-process arithmetic helper; no schema, migration or configuration surface exists in this project.

The changed code path is already covered by an existing test, unlike 0001/0002 at the same phase: test_percent_zero_whole_raises (tests/test_calc.py:20-22, present on HEAD before this change) already calls percent(1, 0) and asserts pytest.raises(ZeroDivisionError) - the exact branch the design modifies. This is a message-only change inside an already-exercised code path, not a new function or a new branch, so the third routine leg ('code the existing tests already cover') holds here where it failed by construction for the two prior sample changes that introduced brand-new public functions.
attempted: Intent: compared intent.md's Proposed outcome (message names 'whole', exception type ZeroDivisionError unchanged, divide's own message unchanged, a test written first and failing before the fix, three green targets) against spec.md's Requirements/Design/Acceptance and plan.md's Order of work/Proof - every bullet is restated with the same substance, nothing added or dropped. Intent's one Open question is answered in spec.md with a stated rationale rather than left open or silently decided without record.

Spec and plan: read spec.md and plan.md end to end. plan.md's Files-that-change order (tests/test_calc.py, then sample_pkg/calc.py) matches its own Order-of-work order (write/fail the test, then implement, then verify); Risks names the riskiest step and the two ways an implementer could depart from the design (omitting `from None`, or a pre-check duplicating divide's condition) and a concrete mitigation for each; Options-not-taken records the three rejected designs and why; Proof lists only named, runnable tests plus the three CLAUDE.md targets. spec.md's header names the skills loaded and 'overrides: none', consistent with sdlc.yaml's protected_paths (empty) and this project having no .claude/skills override files.

Proof: phase (b) is design-only; the diff (diff-b.patch) touches only spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml and this change's evidence/* - no sample_pkg/*.py or tests/*.py yet, which is correct per definition-of-done's phase-b checklist (no build/test/lint log expected at this phase). Read sample_pkg/calc.py and tests/test_calc.py at HEAD to confirm the design's premises: divide(a, b) raises ZeroDivisionError only on b == 0 (no other path through percent's arithmetic can trigger it, so catching ZeroDivisionError in percent cannot mask an unrelated error), percent has no internal callers besides the test module, and mean() goes through divide directly rather than through percent, so mean's tests are unaffected by this design as plan.md and spec.md both state.

Blast radius: confirmed via the diff's own paths and a direct read of status.yaml/sdlc.yaml that nothing outside changes/0015-name-the-zero-whole-in-percent-s-error/** is touched by this phase, no guardrail file is in the diff, and sdlc.yaml's risk_list (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) does not apply to this change.

Policies: spec.md's per-skill rows match the skill texts read directly (coding-standards rule 2 cited for the catch-and-reraise idiom choice over a pre-check; rule 4 cited for the fail-first test; ux-conventions and data-conventions correctly marked not applicable - this is a library exception, not a UI surface or stored data; security-baseline correctly reduced to 'no new dependency' since there is no endpoint, secret or external input). CLAUDE.md's 'Things Claude gets wrong' entry about stale Layout entries is explicitly addressed in both spec.md's Design and plan.md's Risks: no public function is added or removed, so no Layout update is needed, and the plan says so rather than staying silent.

Tests: test_percent_zero_whole_raises and test_divide_by_zero_raises already exist on HEAD and already exercise the exact branches this design touches (percent's zero-whole path, divide's zero-b path); the design keeps both green by construction (exception type unchanged, divide's message unchanged). The planned new test asserts the literal message string, which cannot pass against the current code (today's message is 'b must not be zero', inherited from divide) - a bug that left the old message in place would fail the new test, so the test is not vacuous. No pre-existing test is weakened, skipped or deleted; change_type is fix and plan.md does not touch tests/test_flag.py or modify any existing assertion.
Skip markers: no skip marker, xfail, skip decorator or pytest.ini exclusion appears anywhere in this diff; plan.md declares none and none is needed at this phase.
Not used as a reason: no deterministic gate/skill check was re-run or cited; the reasons above rest on reading intent.md, spec.md, plan.md, sdlc.yaml, REVIEW.md, calc.py and test_calc.py directly.
